reason: The source changes implement persistent simplex edge-weight state, incremental DSE updates, and preservation through basis reinversion/backtracking. These are core pivot-pricing and solver-work mechanisms. The author’s performance statement is not treated as admission evidence. The task will fix the DSE pricing strategy to the documented Steepest Edge mode so the reviewed code path is mandatory.
solver_behavior_hypothesis: With dual steepest-edge pricing fixed on, maintaining edge-weight state and incrementally updating it after pivots may reduce full recomputation and alter pivot choices. The effect depends on repeated DSE pivots and basis updates; stale or incorrectly scaled weights can instead degrade pricing or numerical behavior.
causal_chain: DSE weights estimate edge lengths for candidate pivots. The PR stores these weights in basis-associated state, permutes/scatters and restores them around reinversion/backtracking, computes them when absent, and updates them after pivots. This can change full DSE recomputation cost, per-pivot updates, pivot sequence, simplex iterations, LP bounds, and MIP node processing.
structural_trigger: LP relaxations solved with simplex_dual_edge_weight_strategy=2 (Steepest Edge) and repeated pivots. Basis reinversion/backtracking is a separate persistence path that must be measured independently. MIP root and node relaxations from the knapsack and scheduling panels are candidate workloads; Devex/primal cases are controls.
activation_probe: Run exact base and PR snapshots with simplex_dual_edge_weight_strategy=2 fixed in task parameters. Count HEkkDual::updateFtranDSE, PR HEkk::computeDualSteepestEdgeWeights and HEkk::updateDualSteepestEdgeWeights, and basis save/restore calls. Confirm the active strategy from the options file. Current public probes show DSE FTRAN and weight-update activity on both families, basis saves, and zero basis restores; do not claim the restore branch is covered. Retain raw traces and solver statuses.
instance_selection_rule: Freeze the ten public knapsack and single-machine scheduling MIP models. Fix simplex_dual_edge_weight_strategy=2 for Agent and Judge so each LP relaxation uses DSE. Stratify by LP relaxation size, sparsity, and baseline proof difficulty. Use one representative per family for source counters and the full panel for correctness; retain every seed, status, timeout, and control outcome.
workload_exposure_plan: Build exact base and PR snapshots offline with the same pinned parent image. Run identical MIP inputs, seeds, budgets, and the fixed simplex_dual_edge_weight_strategy=2 setting; retain effective parameter files, source counters for DSE updates/recomputations, reinversions, and backtracking. Do not use coding-agent outcomes or the PR author’s performance claim as admission evidence.
mathematical_risk: Incorrect weight restoration, scaling, or update arithmetic can mis-rank pivots, cause cycling or numerical instability, invalidate a dual bound, or corrupt solver statuses.
independent_check_plan: Independently verify returned incumbents against original MIP constraints/objectives; compare proven optima and dual bounds on tractable cases. Exercise degenerate LPs, reinversion/backtracking cases, and both DSE and Devex controls. Preserve all failures and timeouts.
hidden_generalization_plan: If activation and correctness gates pass, measure fixed-budget solved coverage, proof time, dual-bound progress, simplex iterations, MIP nodes, and peak memory on held-out knapsack and scheduling MIPs, stratified by DSE activation. Report all regressions and timeouts; report the human PR outcome separately.
overlap_review: Existing HiGHS tasks cover MIP primal heuristics, branching, cut generation/aging, presolve, and bound repair at distinct source snapshots. This PR targets simplex edge-weight state and DSE pricing at the Jan 2022 snapshot, a separate mechanism and source lineage within HiGHS.
resource_risk: Persistent edge-weight vectors add state memory; DSE updates and consistency checks can add per-pivot work. Record both recomputation/update counts and end-to-end solver outcomes.
